strings.name: Andrés Manuel López Obrador
strings.role: Former president of Mexico and founder of Morena
strings.summary: López Obrador led the Party of the Democratic Revolution and Mexico City's government before helping turn Morena into a political party. He served as president of Mexico from 2018 to 2024. His government expanded cash transfers and raised the minimum wage; judicial reform and the distribution of power among state institutions generated continuing debate.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through 18 November 2026. His presidential term has ended. Recent activity is supported by reporting on a social-media message on 28 October 2026; birthday greetings are not treated as evidence of an in-person appearance.
strings.influence.rationale: Founded Morena and was elected president of Mexico; his social welfare, energy and infrastructure policies had nationwide influence.
strings.facts.f1.label: Higher education
strings.facts.f1.value: Licenciatura in political science and public administration from the National Autonomous University of Mexico. An indexed extract of the university bulletin confirms the award on 12 November 1987.
strings.facts.f2.label: Three presidential campaigns
strings.facts.f2.value: Contested the 2006, 2012 and 2018 presidential elections, winning on his third attempt. His self-proclamation as 'legitimate president' in 2006 was not a constitutional inauguration.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Changing welfare and wage policy
strings.highlights.h1.text: His administration expanded direct cash transfers and promoted real increases in the minimum wage. An International IDEA review credits these policies with contributing to poverty reduction while describing overall economic performance as mixed.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Advocating elected judges
strings.highlights.h2.text: Supported electing judges, arguing that the reform would serve ordinary citizens. Critics feared damage to political independence. The reform's provisions are distinguished from competing assessments of their effects.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Issued a condolence message after leaving office
strings.timeline.t1.text: El Financiero reported his social-media tribute to Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas and assessment of his political contribution. This documents a written message, not attendance at an event.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Presidential term ended
strings.timeline.t2.text: Completed the term that began on 1 December 2018; Claudia Sheinbaum succeeded him the following day. The legal last day of his term is distinguished from the handover date.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Published the judicial reform decree
strings.timeline.t3.text: Signed and published the decree establishing judicial elections. Transitional provisions made it effective the following day, 16 September; publication day was not the date of the judicial elections.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Took office as president of Mexico
strings.timeline.t4.text: Was sworn in after winning the 2018 election and receiving Electoral Tribunal confirmation. His electoral coalition included Morena, the Labor Party and the Social Encounter Party.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Morena was granted party registration
strings.timeline.t5.text: The national electoral authority approved registration as a national political party, effective from 1 August. This is distinct from the movement's earlier formation.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Became head of the Federal District government
strings.timeline.t6.text: Began leading the government of what was then Mexico's Federal District, serving until July 2005 before pursuing the presidency.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Led the Party of the Democratic Revolution
strings.timeline.t7.text: Became the party's national president, serving until 1999. This preceded his later leadership work in Morena.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Earned a degree in political science and public administration
strings.timeline.t8.text: According to an indexed extract of the UNAM bulletin, he earned his licenciatura after fulfilling university requirements. Earlier years of study are distinct from the degree award date.
